text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
NOWA EUROPA

Poland's opposition nationalist rightist Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) criticised the co-ruling Polish Peasant Party (PSL) over the government's agricultural policies. ROP, struggling to boost its rating before this year's parliamentary elections, said PSL was not a true representative of farmers' interests.
ZYCIE

- The parliamentary committee working on a draft of Poland's new constitution decided that the members of parliament will not be allowed to work at the president's office, act as deputy ministers or head central institutions. They will be allowed to join the government as ministers. The parliamentary committee dropped a proposal by the Solidarity to ban abortion in the constitution.
ECONIOMIC AND MARKET NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's mining sector restructuring programme, drafted by deputy economy minister Jerzy Markowski, envisages rescheduling payments of the mines' nine billion zloty debt and forgiving most interest on the debt. It would also introduce the so-called coal fee, at 3.7 percent of the value of acquired coal, levied on coal buyers.
- The International Monetary Fund's (IMF) representative in Polans Markus Rodlauer said Poland's trade deficit, which reached $12.6 billion in 1996, was no reason for panic .
- The central bank is likely to cut interest rates in the next few months or in the second half of the year, Poland's Finance Minister Marek Belka said.

- Germany's GEC Alsthom, which acquired a 60 percent stake in the Chorzow-based Konstal rolling stock maker in southern Poland, will invest 50 million zlotys in the next two years to modernise the factory and integrate it with the concern's other plants, Konstal's supervisory board president Hans-Jurgen Jabs said.
- Digital mobile phone operator Era GSM has contracted equipment deliveries from Siemens and Ericsson to develop a network in the Gdansk province, northern Poland, this year.

- The listed Rafako boiler maker will construct desulphurisation facilities on two energy blocks of the Belchatow power plant. The ABB-Zamech energy equipment maker will modernise the 18K360 turbine of the plant.

- Representatives of all Polish insurance firms have gathered on a two-day conference to discuss problems of the industry such as capital acquisition, legislative changes and threats thay will face after Poland opens its insurance market to foreign competition in 1999, the Polish Insurance Chamber (PIU) president Jerzy Wysocki said.
NOWA EUROPA
- The Szczecin shipyard has contracted construction of 58 vessels worth $1.5 billion to be built in the next few years, the yard's spokesman Wojciech Sobecki said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Korea's Il Jeong Industrial car upholstery maker has paid $1 million to buy a controlling stake in the Lodz-based Vera textile plant from the National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 11, the Fund's president Ireneusz Nawrocki said.
- France's EDF energy concern is planning to take over the Krakow heating and power plant, the company said. The plant made a net profit of 24 million zloty on revenues of 255 million zlotys in 1996.
ZYCIE
- The listed Okocim breweries have acquired a licence to produce Carlsberg beer and will introduce the new brand on the market in summer this year, Okocim said.
PARKIET
- Plastic maker Stilon, controlled by the NFI No. 2, will invest 120 million zlotys by 2003 to modernise, the company said. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
